notes.key_messages: Questions requiring candidates to plan an investigation should be answered with details of the apparatus to be used. The practical procedures should be clearly specified and candidates should provide a conclusion. Candidates are advised to write preliminary notes before starting to write the plan. Candidates should use a sharp pencil for plotting points and for drawing lines of best fit on their graphs. The line of best fit might be a curve or a straight line. Straight lines should be drawn with a ruler, but rulers should not be used to join the points on a curve. Lines of best fit should avoid anomalous points. Candidates are advised to read the questions thoroughly.
notes.general_comments: The majority of candidates attempted all of the questions. Most candidates were able to complete the tables of results from readings on diagrams and plot points successfully on a grid. Candidates found Questions 1, 2(d)(e), 3(g) and 6 to be the most demanding. Some candidates had difficulty understanding the instructions given in questions. This was particularly noticeable in Question 1(e)(iii).
notes.1a: Most candidates scored both marks for identifying the pipette and burette.
notes.1b: Many good answers were seen, for example referring to methyl orange or litmus. The use of Universal Indicator showed a lack of practical experience with titrations.
notes.1c: This question was generally well answered with candidates achieving full credit.
notes.1di: The type of chemical reaction was usually correctly identified. Incorrect answers included redox, displacement and endothermic.
notes.1dii: Common incorrect responses were “the formation of a precipitate” or “no more fizzing”.
notes.1ei: The anomalous result in experiment 2 was correctly identified.
notes.1eii: About half of the candidates correctly identified that there was a measuring or recording error.
notes.1eiii: A significant number of candidates did not follow the instruction and averaged all four results. Some candidates omitted the unit.
notes.1f: Only the better-performing candidates understood that the hydrochloric acid was more concentrated as a smaller volume of it was needed to react completely with the 25.0 cm of aqueous sodium hydroxide. Most candidates misunderstood the question and identified one of the four experiments as being the most concentrated.
notes.2a: This question was generally well answered.
notes.2b: The majority of candidates answered correctly. Inappropriate methods, such as using a spatula or brush, showed a lack of understanding of practical techniques. Common answers were pen/pencil/ink and a locating agent; this showed that more careful reading of the question was needed.
notes.2d: Only the better-performing candidates understood that compound Q was insoluble in the solvent and therefore remained on the baseline. Many incorrect responses focussed on the density of Q; discussed the composition of Q; or just stated that Q had a low R value.
notes.2e: This question was generally well answered. A number of candidates were unable to follow the guidance given. It appeared that some candidates did not have a ruler or electronic calculator.
notes.3a: Completing the table of temperature readings was done extremely well by candidates.
notes.3b: The points on the graph were usually correctly plotted although a few candidates got the y-axis scale wrong and some candidates missed points out. Some lines of best fit were not smooth curves and some candidates drew straight lines through all the points. A number of candidates, despite identifying the inaccurate point in (c), included it on their line of best fit.
notes.3c: The vast majority of candidates spotted the inaccurate point and explained that it was not on the smooth curve.
notes.3d: This question was generally well answered. Errors included misreading the value from the y-axis; reading the starting value from the x-axis; or drawing an incorrect tie line. Some candidates missed the unit out or gave it incorrectly.
notes.3ei: Most candidates specified that the rate of reaction would increase as the temperature increased. A significant minority of candidates confused rate with reaction time.
notes.3eii: Many correct answers to this question were seen. It was necessary to refer to rate of reaction, rather than reaction time, in the answer.
notes.3fi: Most candidates scored credit for this question.
notes.3fii: Many correct sketch curves were seen. Some candidates did not attempt this question.
notes.3g: Better-performing candidates were able to communicate the idea that the purpose of the cotton wool was to prevent the escape or splashing of acid and to allow the carbon dioxide gas to escape. Common misconceptions were that the cotton wool prevented gas escaping and stopped air entering the flask.
notes.5c: Credit was awarded for understanding that copper ions were present. Full credit was awarded for copper chloride though many other copper compounds were mentioned by candidates.
notes.5d: Many candidates thought that a precipitate or solid would be observed, despite the fact that this was solution L. Only a minority of candidates described the solution correctly as colourless. Yellow and white were common incorrect responses.
notes.5ei: Many candidates incorrectly stated that the precipitate was soluble or that effervescence was seen.
notes.5eii: Many incorrect references to the formation of a white precipitate were seen. A large number of incomplete answers were also seen.
notes.5eiii: Common incorrect responses were white precipitate or no precipitate.
